title: Interfay Sealing and Corrosion Protection Improvement of the Fwd Lower Shell Longitudinal Lap Joints
abstract: Restoration of the corrosion protection of the forward lower shell longitudinal lap joints by re-sealing the faying surfaces and replacing the aft splice plate, addressing filiform corrosion found under the fastener heads on early classic aircraft.

sections.reason: Filiform and exfoliation corrosion was reported on the longitudinal lap joints of the forward lower shell on aircraft in their third decade of service, principally where the cargo compartment floor drains discharge onto the lower shell. Twenty-nine findings were recorded across a population of roughly 480 early classic aircraft between 2013 and 2016. In every case the interfay sealant had degraded and moisture had reached the faying surface between the two skin sheets. Blend-out inside the allowable limits was possible on most aircraft, but four cases had already reached the limit and required an engineering repair.
sections.description: The joint is opened locally between stations 1080 and 1360 on both sides of the lower shell, the existing aft splice plate ORV288354-46 is removed, and the faying surfaces are cleaned and re-treated to the surface protection standard of ATA 51-20. A new chromate-inhibited interfay sealant bead is applied along the full joint length and the joint is re-fastened wet with rivets AES645587-2A. The lower shell clip D5321122023477 is retained where its condition permits and renewed where corrosion has reduced the flange thickness beyond the blend limit. Access is from inside the forward and aft cargo compartments, zones 113 and 121, with the cargo floor panels and the lower lining removed between the two frame stations. Drawing D53211223480 issue H carries the revised joint detail and the fastener pattern.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 1.8 kg per aircraft, symmetric about the aircraft centre line, with no measurable centre-of-gravity effect. No electrical load change. The re-sealed joint is interchangeable with the previous standard; a mixed configuration between the left and right sides of one aircraft is acceptable. The corrosion-prevention and control programme task for this zone remains applicable but its interval is doubled once the modification is embodied. Manual content for ATA 53-21 is under review and the affected tasks and figures will be re-issued alongside the modification.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only. Embodiment takes approximately three days with the cargo compartments already stripped, and is normally combined with a scheduled structural check. Kits are built against firm orders with a fourteen week lead time, and the first sets are released to the launch operator whose findings raised the dossier.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric installation, no measurable CG effect
type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in; the affected build standard was out of production before release
